findings.title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting() can break the $__range guard and split queries with a baked-in full range
findings.body: querySupportsSplitting() (line 282-289) relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) to detect `$__range` and exclude those queries from time splitting, with an explicit comment saying `$__range` must be interpolated on the backend with the split time range. This PR now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on every target before that check runs. If template interpolation resolves a `$__range` reference (e.g. scopedVars carries the range variables, so `$__range` becomes a fixed duration of the *original* full range), isQueryWithRangeVariable() no longer matches: the query is no longer excluded, and it gets split into day-long chunks while the expression still contains the full-range duration. Each sub-request then computes over the whole original range instead of the split range, producing wrong results — exactly the failure mode the existing comment warns about. Either applyTemplateVariables must be guaranteed not to resolve range variables, or the range-variable check must be done on the pre-interpolation expr.

findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice in the shard-splitting path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() now maps targets through datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (line 52), but it then delegates execution to runSplitQuery() (line 163), which in this same PR was changed to call datasource.applyTemplateVariables() again on every target of the request it receives (querySplitting.ts line 299). Every query is therefore interpolated twice (the updated shard test even asserts 5 calls for a single target). Template interpolation is not guaranteed idempotent: if a variable's value itself contains `$`-like syntax (e.g. a label value or regex with `$`), or if the interpolation of step/expr is not a pure function of the input, the second pass can mangle the expression or step. The duplicated interpolation should be removed from one of the two layers, or runSplitQuery should be given a way to skip interpolation for already-interpolated targets.
